scope: New registry/proposals/ entry (registry/proposals/flood_burden_ledger.json, PROP-FLOOD-05a and PROP-FLOOD-05b, amended per independent review GO_WITH_FIXES): two method-domain (M) proposals for a community flood-readout application (FloodConnect), via the governed proposals-lane intake process -- NOT promoted into registry/CANONICAL.json, which requires the full schema/lineage/checker workflow these entries have not gone through. PROP-FLOOD-05a is a control-structure burden readout: for a declared structure c between sides A/B (with a declared side-to-zone map zeta(c,A), zeta(c,B)) with gauged levels h_A(t), h_B(t) and a declared state g_c(t) in {OPEN, CLOSED, PUMPING}, it is a total function with refusal rows (UNDECLARED_STRUCTURE > MISSING_INPUT/STALE_INPUT > DATUM_MISMATCH > CONTROL_STATE_MISSING) checked before gate-state rows; when OPEN the gradient-direction readout is declared inapplicable and defers to PROP-FLOOD-04 (a pending sibling proposal, PR #61, flagged as such); when CLOSED or PUMPING the higher-level side reads HIGHER_SIDE (term of art BURDENED), the lower LOWER_SIDE (RELIEVED), else UNRESOLVED. A persistence count P_c(k) is registered as a NEW construction of this proposal (PROP-FLOOD-01 is cited only for shared tick/epsilon discipline, not as the source of a persistence count), reported alongside, never converted into a motive/fault/blame claim; an explicit caveat states that under PUMPING(A->B) the receiving side can still read RELIEVED, since the labels read level, not transfer. EQ-001/C.01.v1 is cited only as an analogy (cites_analogy), not as a generalised parent. PROP-FLOOD-05b (renamed from 'protection-order' to 'net-relief count ordering' for neutrality) aggregates 05a's boundary readouts per declared zone (via zeta) into R(Z,t)-B(Z,t) plus a signed tie-break SigmaP_rel(Z,t)-SigmaP_bur(Z,t) (never a same-sign sum), producing a dense rank (ties share one rank value, never broken by name/id) among evaluable zones; UNRESOLVED/GRADIENT_ONLY boundaries are declared neutral (count toward neither R nor B); zones with a REFUSED boundary get their own NO_ORDER list, zones with an undeclared/empty boundary set get their own separate NOT_EVALUABLE list -- the two are never merged. 05b drops EQ-001/C.01.v1 entirely and cites PROP-FLOOD-03's gate_flag construction as the precedent for gating an aggregate on a declared boundary state instead. Both entries are tier Dr / status unverified, carry explicit claim_boundary/honest_caveats stating the readout is of measured consequence only, never an intent/policy/fairness judgement, and that tide can produce the same gauged asymmetry as a closed gate (the declared control state, not the asymmetry itself, licenses the reading). empirical_test_status is 'none' for both. No claim about the Clay Millennium Navier-Stokes problem, or about any object's Clay/NS status, is made or implied anywhere in this change; the status of every existing Clay-related registry object (CANONICAL.json, coq/, docs/CLAY_*) is unchanged -- this PR touches no such object, only adds one new proposals-lane file.
